turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to start learning a new language this year.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Great goal. Is there a language you need for work or travel, or would you rather pick one just because it sounds fun?

think_reask: So, have you picked a language? Something useful, or just for fun?
Time's up. Which language is calling to you?
Any ideas yet? Work, travel, or just for the joy of it?
welcome_back: Welcome back! You were picking a language to learn this year.
Hi again. Have you thought about which language you'd like to start?
There you are. So, which language are we going with?

endings.user: Italian. We're going to Rome next spring.
endings.moshi: Perfect. Start with travel phrases and food vocabulary, you'll use those constantly.

endings.user: Japanese, honestly just because I love the culture.
endings.moshi: Wonderful. Learn the two kana alphabets first, they make everything else easier.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've been doing Spanish on an app for months, but I still freeze when someone talks to me.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Very common. Would you be up for weekly sessions with an online tutor, or does a casual language exchange sound better?

think_reask: So, for speaking practice, a tutor or a language exchange?
Okay, ready? Paid tutor, or a free exchange partner?
Have you decided how you want to practice talking?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were choosing between a tutor and a language exchange for your Spanish.
Hi again. So, tutor or exchange partner?
Good to have you back. Any decision on how to practice speaking Spanish?

endings.user: A tutor. I need someone to actually correct me.
endings.moshi: Good thinking. Even thirty minutes a week with corrections makes a big difference.

endings.user: The exchange, I'd rather not pay right now.
endings.moshi: Fair enough. Split the time evenly, half in Spanish and half in English.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My French exam is in two months.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Okay, let's plan. How much time can you realistically give it each day, and which part worries you most, grammar, listening or speaking?

contexts.pending: daily study time and weakest skill
think_reask: So, how much time per day, and what's your weak spot?
Time's up. Tell me your daily study time and the part that worries you most.
Ready? Grammar, listening or speaking, and how many minutes a day?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were planning your French exam prep. How much time a day, and what's hardest?
Hi again. Have you figured out your study time and your weakest skill?
There you are. So, for the French exam, what worries you most?

endings.user: About an hour a day, and listening is the worst.
endings.moshi: Then spend half of it on French podcasts or news with transcripts. Listen first, then read along.

endings.user: Maybe twenty minutes, and grammar scares me.
endings.moshi: That's enough if you're steady. Do one grammar topic a week with short daily exercises.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, how do you say I'm hungry in German again?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Ich habe Hunger. Literally, I have hunger.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's so weird. Why not just I am hungry?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Same with thirst. Lots of languages do it that way.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, ich habe Hunger. Did I say it right?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Pretty close. Make the H a bit softer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Are you still going to that conversation group on Thursdays?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Yeah, at the library. It's mostly retirees, but they're really nice.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do they let beginners join?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure. Last week a guy only knew how to order coffee and they loved him.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ha, that's basically my level. Can I come with you next week?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Of course. Bring a notebook, they throw a lot of new words at you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you quiz me on these flashcards for a minute?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure. What's the word for window?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ventana.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Correct. And spoon?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Uh, cuchillo?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: No, that's knife. Spoon is cuchara.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I always mix those two up. Can you do the kitchen ones again?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's the fastest way to build vocabulary in a new language?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Spaced repetition flashcards are hard to beat. Ten or fifteen minutes a day, every day, works better than long weekend sessions.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I learn random words or follow a list?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Start with the most common few hundred words. They cover a surprisingly large chunk of everyday conversation.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And I've heard that reading helps but / I'm not sure what to read as a beginner.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try graded readers. They're short books written with simple vocabulary for learners at your level.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh nice, I didn't know those existed.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: They're great. Children's books work too, though some use oddly specific words like dragon or castle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it too late to learn a language at fifty?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all. Adults often learn grammar and vocabulary faster than kids, they just take longer with the accent.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My accent is going to be awful.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Maybe a little, but people care much more about whether they understand you. A clear accent beats a perfect one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fair. I was thinking Portuguese, or / maybe Greek, since we go there every summer.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Greek would be lovely if you visit every year, you'd get real practice each trip. The alphabet takes a week or two to learn, then it's fine.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, Greek it is. Where do I start?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Learn the alphabet first, then basic greetings and food words. Locals really appreciate even a little effort.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Does watching shows in another language actually help?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It does, especially for listening. Subtitles in the target language help more than subtitles in your own.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: But I can't follow anything without English subtitles yet.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then start with shows you've already seen. Knowing the story lets you focus on the words.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good idea. How many episodes a week / should I aim for?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Two or three, watched actively, is plenty. Pause and repeat lines out loud now and then.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll try that with a Korean drama I loved.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect choice. Dramas repeat lots of everyday phrases, so you'll pick them up quickly.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm trying to choose how to learn Spanish this year, and I'd love some advice.
options: The first option is an evening class at the community college, twice a week, for about three hundred dollars.
Then there's an app subscription, which is cheap and I could do it on my commute.
And the last one is a two-week immersion trip to Mexico, living with a host family.
moshi_comment: The immersion trip would give you the most speaking practice by far, but two weeks alone won't stick without some groundwork. The evening class gives you structure and a teacher who corrects you. What's your budget?
I'd combine them if you can. Use the app daily for vocabulary, and pick the class for speaking. The trip makes a great goal for later in the year.

option_sets.lead_in: My company will pay for one language course, and I'm not sure which language to pick.
options: First, there's German, since our biggest client is in Munich.
Next, Mandarin, which would look great on my resume but seems really hard.
Or there's French, which I studied in school, so I wouldn't start from zero.
Finally, Arabic, because we might open an office in Dubai next year.
moshi_comment: German seems the most immediately useful, since you'd actually talk to that client. Mandarin is impressive, but it takes years to reach a working level. How long does the course last?
French would give you the fastest progress because of your school background. Still, if the Dubai office really happens, Arabic could set you apart. How certain is that plan?
